# Microsoft Azure ServiceNetworking management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Service Networking provides managing of following fully managed azure services:

- Traffic Controller: Fully managed Azure Service which provides L7 Load Balancing and Dynamic Traffic Management capabilities for container workloads. Traffic Controller extends Azure's L7 Load Balancing portfolio and is offered as new SKU under Application Gateway product family.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure ServiceNetworking management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.ServiceNetworking
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html)

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: The Custom partial defines the cited editor-hidden overload and forwards the old nullable provisioning-state argument to the expanded factory signature. Its legacy-overload pattern and model-factory classification fit the captured code.

The obsolete Custom factory really defaults null tags, converts nonnull subnetId to WritableSubResource, and constructs the legacy AssociationData. This is a separate handwritten model factory instance.
The obsolete FrontendData factory in Custom defaults null tags and invokes the legacy constructor with null additional raw data; its cited lines and model-factory classification match.

The Custom overload maps a flattened WAF identifier into a conditional SecurityPolicyConfigurations object, defaults private endpoint connections, and forwards the other arguments. The factory pattern describes its reusable shape.
The editor-hidden security-policy factory in Custom retains a signature without rules and forwards rules: default; this is a concrete compatibility overload, not a generated-only annotation.
The editor-hidden frontend factory forwards to the expanded signature with securityPolicyConfigurations: null. The complete implementation and identity are visible in the cited Custom source.

The Custom factory constructs nested AssociationProperties conditionally, distinct from the other factory adapters. Although its optional parameters permit inputs for which associationType.Value would throw, the proposal explicitly does not claim that every combination is safe.

The Custom declaration retains an obsolete, editor-hidden public legacy collection and names its replacement. This is observable API-surface retention/deprecation; the cited declaration supports the finding without assuming the rest of the collection was captured.

The Custom constructor explicitly selects an API version by resource type with a literal fallback and wires a REST client. The novel pattern describes version lookup rather than unsupported version validation; no claim about current emitter capabilities is needed.

The cited Custom method conditionally checks the parent resource type and throws; the Conditional("DEBUG") annotation is material, so the proposal appropriately avoids asserting unconditional release-build validation.

The handwritten sync/async methods adapt the legacy input and initiate typed LROs, but the catalog's lro-operation-wrapper describes a separate handwritten public operation type with wait/result methods; no such type implementation is captured. Use a shape-specific LRO-start adapter pattern instead and avoid claiming custom polling.

finding.explanation: The Custom collection's sync and async CreateOrUpdate methods convert AssociationData into TrafficControllerAssociationData request content, send the request, construct ServiceNetworkingArmOperation<AssociationResource> using AssociationOperationSource and OperationFinalStateVia.AzureAsyncOperation, and wait when waitUntil is Completed. The underlying polling implementation is not shown.
finding.handwrittenRationale: Both complete request/model-adapting LRO startup methods are in the deprecated Custom collection outside Generated; the captured code supports the adapters, not a claim that the operation source or poller itself is handwritten.

decisions.reason: Both complete GET methods convert a response into the current data type, reject a null model and return a legacy AssociationResource via AssociationData while preserving the raw response. The result-projection pattern fits.

The paired list methods visibly wrap their collection results with a per-item AssociationData-to-AssociationResource projection. This is paging item projection, not evidence that the skipped collection-result classes implement custom next-link behavior.

The captured async method explicitly maps 200 and 404 to a nullable model result and returns a presence boolean, throwing for other statuses. The synchronous counterpart starts at the excerpt boundary, so this finding correctly covers only ExistsAsync.
The Custom model declaration retains the obsolete, editor-hidden AssociationData contract and names the replacement; deprecation of this public legacy model is distinct from its conversion methods.

The captured internal constructor maps current association data into legacy fields, including a wrapped subnet identifier and converted enum/state strings. The source supports the adapter but not assumptions about uncaptured generated model declarations.

The cited conversion method conditionally constructs AssociationProperties, parses the association type, copies subnet only inside that branch and constructs current data. It does not read the legacy ProvisioningState; this is distinct from the reverse constructor adapter.

The captured public SubnetId getter projects a nested Subnet.Id and the setter creates the nested WritableSubResource if absent. This handwritten flattened property is separately observable from the model conversion methods.

limitations: Coverage is partial: 3 of 190 eligible files from 213 discovered files are supplied. Twenty-seven skipped entries include the AssociationCollection remainder after line 445 and twenty-six wholly unsent Custom files. The collection ends just inside the synchronous Exists try block; its status handling and any later members are not captured, so the complete ExistsAsync finding does not cover its sync counterpart.

The underlying REST client, common ServiceNetworkingArmOperation implementation, AssociationOperationSource, collection-result classes and pageable-wrapper internals are not supplied. The source establishes custom LRO startup/wait selection and explicit paged item projection, not a handwritten polling engine, custom next-link behavior or the operation source's final-result implementation.

Generated partials, destination factory overloads, current model definitions and most serialization files are absent. Actual wire formats, generated-vs-historical API differences, serializer handling of the raw-data field, and factory overload resolution beyond the shown expressions are not independently established.

The association factory's conditional reads associationType.Value whenever any of the three association inputs is nonnull, rather than separately guarding associationType. The inbound legacy-model constructor constructs a ResourceIdentifier from data.SubnetId without a local null guard. The outbound adapter creates properties only with AssociationType.HasValue and does not read legacy ProvisioningState; no claim that these adapters preserve every value or safely handle every null combination is made.

ValidateResourceId is Conditional("DEBUG"), not unconditional release validation. EditorBrowsable(Never) does not remove public API. Compatibility warnings and comments do not prove current emitter limitations or historic behavior; generatorAddressable yes is a plausible general feature opportunity, not supported current capability.

Routine diagnostics scopes, request-context plumbing, simple scalar state storage and base/state-restoring constructors are treated as parts of the shown retained types and operation adapters, not independent policy customizations. No package-wide absence or completeness conclusion is supported.

Only three Custom source files were captured from 190 eligible files; 26 listed paths were not sent at all and AssociationCollection.cs ends at line 445 in the middle of Exists. These decisions cannot establish the package-wide presence, absence, or completeness of customizations.

The collection-result, operation-source, serialization, resource and generated source implementations were not supplied. Their paging, polling, serialization and generated-versus-handwritten behavior cannot be assessed from these references alone.
Generator addressability is a plausible generalization judgment, not evidence of current emitter or TypeSpec support; generated counterparts and historical motivations were not supplied.
